summary: Clarifies how to compute the length of the Segment ID sub-TLVs defined in RFC 8287 for LSP Ping and Traceroute in Segment Routing. The original text was ambiguous about the Length field, which led to inconsistent implementations.

eli5.summary: A form had a box whose size was unclear, and people filled it in differently. This note says exactly how to count so everyone matches.

questions: what is the length of the ipv4 igp-prefix segment id sub-tlv
how is igp-adjacency sid sub-tlv length calculated
subtitle: Pins down exactly what number goes in the Length field of the Segment ID sub-TLVs from RFC 8287.

tldr.problem: RFC 8287 did not sufficiently clarify how to compute the Length field of its three Segment ID sub-TLVs, which resulted in interoperability issues.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 8690 states the required length for each sub-TLV: 8 for IPv4 IGP-Prefix, 20 for IPv6 IGP-Prefix, and a table of values for IGP-Adjacency.
tldr.outcome: Implementations now have one explicit rule for each sub-TLV, and the length of each MUST be calculated as this RFC defines.

today: RFC 8690 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 8287. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: The Ambiguity Being Fixed
sections.content:
RFC 8287 defines extensions to MPLS LSP Ping and Traceroute for Segment Routing IGP-Prefix and IGP-Adjacency Segment Identifiers (SIDs) with the MPLS data plane. It proposes three Target FEC Stack sub-TLVs.

RFC 8287 defines their format and handling, but it does not sufficiently clarify how to compute the value that goes in each sub-TLV's Length field. That ambiguity may result in interoperability issues. The acknowledgements credit the investigation of the problem to testing at the European Advanced Network Test Center (EANTC).

RFC 8690 updates RFC 8287 by clarifying the length of each Segment ID sub-TLV. Readers are expected to know the terms from RFC 8402, RFC 8029 and RFC 8287.
sections.eli5: Two computers were supposed to write the same number in one box, but the instructions were fuzzy. This note fixes the instructions.

sections.title: The Rule
sections.content:
Section 5 of RFC 8287 defines three Segment ID sub-TLVs that can appear in the Target FEC Stack TLV defined in RFC 8029. The length of each sub-TLV MUST be calculated as RFC 8690 defines.

The TLV drawings in Sections 5.1, 5.2 and 5.3 of RFC 8287 are updated so that they contain explicitly defined lengths.
sections.eli5: The rule is simple: when you fill in the length box, use the exact number this note gives.

sections.title: The IGP-Prefix Sub-TLVs
sections.content:
The sub-TLV length for the IPv4 IGP-Prefix Segment ID (type 34) MUST be set to 8. It holds an IPv4 prefix, a Prefix Length, a Protocol and a Reserved field.

The sub-TLV length for the IPv6 IGP-Prefix Segment ID (type 35) MUST be set to 20. It has the same layout with an IPv6 prefix in place of the IPv4 one.
sections.eli5: For these two kinds of note, the length is always the same fixed number, one for the shorter address type and one for the longer.

sections.title: The IGP-Adjacency Sub-TLV
sections.content:
The length of the IGP-Adjacency Segment ID sub-TLV (type 36) varies with the Adjacency Type and the Protocol. In every allowed combination, the length MUST be calculated by including the 2 octets of the Reserved field.

Table 1 of the RFC lists the result. For OSPF it is 20 for Parallel, IPv4 and Unnumbered adjacencies and 44 for IPv6. For ISIS it is 24 for Parallel, IPv4 and Unnumbered and 48 for IPv6. For Protocol set to Any it is 20, 20, 44 and 20 for Parallel, IPv4, IPv6 and Unnumbered.

The RFC gives an example with Adj. Type set to Parallel Adjacency and Protocol set to 0, which has a Length of 20.
sections.eli5: This kind of note changes size depending on the type of link, so there is a small chart. Look up your link type and use the number in the chart.

sections.title: IANA Considerations
sections.content: IANA listed RFC 8690 as an additional reference for three entries in the "Sub-TLVs for TLV Types 1, 16, and 21" registry: sub-type 34 (IPv4 IGP-Prefix Segment ID), 35 (IPv6 IGP-Prefix Segment ID) and 36 (IGP-Adjacency Segment ID). Each entry keeps its Section 5 reference to RFC 8287.
sections.eli5: The official list of note types now also points to this clarification, so people looking up each type find it.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: RFC 8690 updates RFC 8287 and does not introduce any additional security considerations.
sections.eli5: Because this note only clears up how to count, it adds no new safety worries.
